cards.explanation: Job's covenant with his eyes keeps him from gazing with desire at a virgin, friends. He says, “How then could I gaze with desire at a virgin?” A covenant is a serious promise, and he made this one with his own eyes. It's a promise about where his eyes go.
The answer is False, friends. Job says, “Does He not see my ways and count my every step?” He isn't complaining that God is distracted. He asks whether God sees his ways and counts his every step.

The word is integrity, friends. Job says, “…let God weigh me with honest scales, that He may know my integrity.” Honest scales means no thumb on the side. Job wants God to weigh the whole thing and see what's there.

Job is swearing that he is innocent, friends. He says, “If I have walked in falsehood or my foot has rushed to deceit…” and then he names what should happen to him if he did. Verse after verse, he puts a promise behind his claim that he didn't. A man who says that is putting his name behind his innocence.
The word is crime, friends. Job calls it “…a heinous crime, an iniquity to be judged.” He doesn't use soft words here. He says plainly that being enticed by his neighbor's wife would be serious.

The fire of being enticed by his neighbor's wife would root out his entire harvest, friends. Job says it's a fire that “…burns down to Abaddon…” and “…would root out my entire harvest.” That's the whole harvest gone. He doesn't treat this as a small thing.

The moment he couldn't face is when God rises to judge, friends. Job asks, “…what will I do when God rises to judge? How will I answer when called to account?” He knows his servants aren't the final word on how he treats them. God is, and Job doesn't want to face that moment with a rejected complaint behind him.

The answer is True, friends. Job asks, “Did not He who made me in the womb also make them? Did not the same One form us in the womb?” The same One made Job and the servants. Job asks it right after talking about his servants' complaints.

The answer is True, friends. Job says, “…from my youth I reared him as would a father, and from my mother’s womb I guided the widow…” That's a long stretch of caring for the fatherless and the widow. Job says it goes back to his youth.

The reason Job names is that he saw he had support in the gate, friends. He says, “…because I saw that I had support in the gate…” That's the reason he names for lifting his hand against the fatherless. He says he saw support in the gate, and that's the only reason he gives.

He says may his arm fall from his shoulder, friends. Job says, “…then may my arm fall from my shoulder and be torn from its socket.” It's a heavy thing to say, and he says it plainly. The arm that would lift against the fatherless is the arm he names.
The answer is False, friends. Job says, “For calamity from God terrifies me, and His splendor I cannot overpower.” That's a man who takes God seriously. He says he can't overpower God's splendor.

The word is hand, friends. Job says, “…if I have rejoiced in my great wealth because my hand had gained so much…” It's the picture of a man patting himself on the back. I know that move, because I do it when a batch comes out pretty.

The reason is that he would have denied God on high, friends. Job says, “…this would also be an iniquity to be judged, for I would have denied God on high.” The sun and moon are beautiful, but Job says giving his heart to them would deny God. His reason is that plain.

The word is mouth, friends. Job says, “I have not allowed my mouth to sin by asking for his life with a curse…” He's saying he did not ask for his enemy's life that way. The word that fits the blank is mouth.

The word is traveler, friends. Job says, “…no stranger had to lodge on the street, for my door has been open to the traveler…” A stranger on the road had a place at his house. I think that's worth more than any sign on a door.

The reason Job names is fear of the crowds, friends. He says, “…because I greatly feared the crowds and the contempt of the clans terrified me, so that I kept silent and would not go outside…” That's a man hiding at home. He's saying he never did that.
The answer is False, friends. Job says, “Here is my signature. Let the Almighty answer me…” He puts his name on it and asks God to answer. A man who wants silence doesn't talk like that.

Job would wear the charges against him like a crown, friends. He says, “Surely I would carry it on my shoulder and wear it like a crown.” Most people would hide a list of charges. Job says he'd wear it like a crown.
The answer is True, friends. Job says, “I would give account of all my steps…” and says he would approach God like a prince. That's a man who's ready to talk. I think it's a bold way to walk in.

The word is payment, friends. Job says, “…if I have devoured its produce without payment or broken the spirit of its tenants…” Taking its produce without payment is the thing he's naming. He puts it in an if, so he's saying he didn't do it.

He wants briers growing instead of wheat, friends. Job says, “…then let briers grow instead of wheat and stinkweed instead of barley.” Briers in place of wheat and stinkweed in place of barley is how he ends his list. Then it says the words of Job are done.
